newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STABLE, SEEN SAME IN QUIET MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STABLE, SEEN SAME IN QUIET MARKET.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar opened stable against the U.S. dollar on Friday, and foreign currency dealers said they expected it to spend the day around the opening levels in a quiet market ahead of a long weekend holiday.

"It's very quiet, and people are just waiting to get away," one dealer said. "I cannot see anything happening today as the market is already in a holiday mood," he said of Monday and Tuesday, when the local financial markets are closed for Heroes' and Defence Forces holidays.
The Zimbabwe dollar started the day at its overnight level of 11.6350/6450 to the U.S. dollar, but it was softer at 18.5000/5500 to sterling from 18.4000/4500.

It was also quoted weaker at 6.2200/2300 versus 6.1995/2180 against the German mark and at 2.4900/5000 against the South African rand from 2.4805/4850, rates which dealers said reflected trends on the overseas markets.
